standard.goal: Given the prompt for a request it is made for, an AI agent does the task as the prompt's writer means, with only what its run gives it, on every run and in cases the writer did not foresee.

parts.what: What the host reads to choose the prompt for a request: a name that says what the prompt does, and a description of what it does and the requests it is used for.
The tools the AI may use, listed where the host reads them and refuses any other, when the host allows such a list.
What the AI reads first in the body: what it is to achieve, for whom, how it knows it is done, and what lies outside its task.
What the AI needs and cannot find or know on its own: the situation, its inputs and where they are, and the rules of this place.
The steps in the order the AI takes them, each step the result that holds when it ends, with the rules the step needs, each with its reason, or the script that does it and how to run it.
What the AI hands back, in what form, and to whom.

checklist.what: When the AI believes it has finished, can it tell from the prompt whether it has reached what the task is for?
When the AI meets a choice that is the user's, such as one between options that serve equally or an action hard to undo, does it hand the choice to the user rather than make it?
Given the prompt and only what its run gives it, can the AI do each step without guessing a fact, such as where its inputs are or a rule of the place it works in?
Taking the steps in order, does the AI arrive at what the goal says the task is for, with no step that leads it elsewhere?
When the AI meets a case a step's rule does not name, can it decide the case as the writer would, from the reason the rule gives?
When the AI is run twice on the same input, does each step whose result must not vary, such as a check or a file's form, give the same result both times?
Can the AI take every action its steps call for with the tools it is allowed?
When the AI, during a run, reaches for an action that lies outside its task, does the host refuse it?
When the caller, the person or the AI that started the prompt, takes what the AI hands back, can it act on it without asking the AI anything further?

When a request the prompt is made for comes, and a request near it that it is not made for, does the host, such as Claude Code, choose the prompt for the first and pass it over for the second, from the name and the description alone?
Once the host has chosen the prompt by its description, does the AI do the task the description says, all of it and nothing more?
When the prompt is run several times on each kind of request it is made for, does the AI reach the result the prompt names on every run?
Does every line of the prompt change what the AI does toward the task, so that none draws its attention from the lines that do?

methods.question: Q1
methods.thinking: The AI stops when its work looks done, so the prompt says what the result is for and gives a check that tells done from looking done.
steps: For each thing that holds once the task is met, give the check that shows it: a command to run where one exists, or else what to look up and where.
Write when the AI stops: once every check passes, or at a blocker it cannot pass, which it hands back with what it found.

methods.question: Q4
methods.thinking: Each step is a result on the way to the goal, so the AI chooses how to reach it and knows when to go on.
steps: Write the steps in the order their results must hold, so the AI sees that order, such as in a numbered list.
Check that a later step or the goal uses each step's result, and cut a step whose result nothing uses.
Check that the last step leaves what the goal says the task is for.

methods.question: Q5
methods.thinking: A rule that says what it is for lets the AI apply it where it was meant and judge a case no rule names, so each rule carries its reason.
steps: Write the rule as what to do, in plain words, with no capitals or warnings for emphasis.
Where a rule says always or never, say what the AI does when the rule cannot be met.
In place of a list of edge cases, give the way of judging and a few typical examples that differ from one another.
Think of a case the rule does not name, read only the rule and its reason, and check that they lead where the writer would go; where they do not, mend the reason.

methods.question: Q7
methods.thinking: Each action a step calls for needs a tool the AI is allowed, or the step cannot be taken however well it is written.

steps: List the actions the task must never take, such as writing where it only reads.
Allow only the tools Q7's list needs.
Where a tool it needs also allows an action it must never take, add a rule the host enforces, such as a deny rule or a hook.

methods.question: Q9
methods.thinking: The caller sees only what comes back, so the prompt says what that is, in what form and to whom, and a step makes each of it.
steps: Name the caller, and what it does next with the result.
List what it needs for that: the result, what was done, and what was not done and why.
Choose the form by who reads it: a fixed form, such as JSON, where a script reads it, and short plain words where a person does.

Hand the output alone to someone in the caller's place, and see whether they can act without asking.
